title: Benny Goodman as a young man in the Pollack band
summary: Freeman says Goodman was kind to him at Pollack's but later, running a big band, grew cruel without awareness.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: But we were talking about the Pollack band, and you said, why did we not get into talking about Pollack.
That was your first experience in a big band with wonderful guys at that time.

Yes, a big band in those days was ten men, and I say, Glenn Miller, Benny Goodman -- and Benny Goodman was so nice to me. I had never sat next to anyone that played that marvelously. And Pollack played the drums.
And Benny was very nice to you?
Oh, Benny Goodman was a marvelous young man.
Is that right? So he wasn't as standoffish and he wasn't --

Oh, Benny Goodman was the finest man you would ever want to meet until he got into the big band thing and had all that pressure on him and nervousness, and I say it is an amazing thing that a man that is as great an artist as he was, could have managed to run a big band, which he did.
I mean, he knew what he was doing and he knew what he wanted and he was like a machine, but when he was cruel, I doubt very much that he was aware of it.
